$comment: The vocabularies a paired client is allowed to put on the wire: event types,
sources, and tool types.
This file exists because each of these was hand-authored twice with no
mechanical link between the copies -- AscendaTelemetryEventType and
AscendaTelemetrySource in ai-engineer-tools' packages/tool-contract (TypeScript),
and WorkloadCategoryMap / KnownSources / KnownToolTypes in
Services/ToolTelemetryCatalog.cs (C#). Drift between them did not fail a build.
It surfaced as rows in the 'unclassified' bucket months later, which is how
@ascenda-one/history-import lost seven months of one person's history behind a
2xx; and as code_forge, which ascenda-github-collector has always sent and
KnownSources never listed, harmless only because IsKnownSource is not consulted
at ingest.
v1 covered eventTypes only, which is precisely why the source drift went
unnoticed when the event-type drift was caught. v2 pins all three.
Ownership: this file is the source of truth for the wire vocabularies. The C#
side pins it in ToolPairingCatalogValidationTests; the TypeScript side should
vendor a copy and assert equality against its unions in its own test, so a name
added on one side and not the other fails a build rather than a dashboard.
Each list is the CLIENT-EMITTABLE set. The C# registries are deliberately
supersets of it:
- eventTypes omits supervision_interruption and the coarse workflow/HRIS types
(email_activity, message_activity, calendar_block), which the org
activity-signals door mints internally via CoarseSignalTypeMap rather than
accepting from a paired client.
- sources omits 'other', which is not a value a client sends but what
NormalizeSource substitutes for a blank one.
Enforcement differs per list, and the difference is deliberate:
- eventTypes IS enforced at ingest; an off-catalog type is rejected per item
with reason unknown_event_type.
- toolTypes IS enforced at pairing; an unknown toolType is a 400.
- sources is NOT enforced at ingest today. IsKnownSource exists and is tested
but is not consulted, so an unrecognised source is accepted and stored as
sent. It does not affect workloadCategory. Before wiring enforcement, audit
live traffic the way the event-type change did -- and note that
ResolveConsentType currently falls back to the ide_telemetry lease for an
unrecognised source, which is a consent question, not a vocabulary one.
